In the 1700s, people in Britain rented pineapples for their parties.
Pineapples didn't grow in Britain. Bringing one from the tropics by ship usually meant it rotted on the way.
So the rich built heated glasshouses to grow them, and it took years to get a single fruit.
One pineapple could cost as much as a new carriage.
Owning one meant you were wealthy. So people who couldn't afford one, rented one.
They'd put it in the middle of the table, or carry it around the party, to impress the guests.
Nobody ate it. The next day, it went back to the shop, and on to the next party.
It only got eaten when it was too old to show off.
One Scottish lord even built a house with a giant stone pineapple on top. It's still standing.
